**Requirement ids:** **SIG-ENG-043** (owner — the trigger-register checker:
one row per revisit trigger, hash/state/evidence/open-home verified, the
round-tail mode the closing rows use) · **SIG-ENG-039** (satisfied —
index fields, appended status lines; the new ADR's Appendix F row lands in
the same change) · B4 **G8** `adr-index-and-triggers` · **COV-14** · **Base:**
`r11/P34.31-living-record-test-lint` (stacked; merge after P34.31) · **Ticket:**
`docs/tickets/237_P34.32__adr-index-generator-and-trigger-register.md`
(manifest row 237 — Round 11 / P34, sub-round 11A; depends SEED-15) ·
**Gate:** no pause · **Live stage:** none (`live_verification=false`) ·
**Production mutations:** none · **CI config changed: no** — the two new
checks join `make docs-check`, which the existing `docs` job already runs.

## Why

The index did not tell the truth: the vendored `adr-index.sh` overrode a
frozen `Accepted` header only for `Superseded by`, so twenty ADRs whose
landed `## Status updates` sections record amendment, qualification,
extension or revisit rendered a lie of omission. Declared relationships
leaked the other way too — later ADRs declared eight relationships the
target ADRs never recorded (COV-14's exactly the "none superseded"
reading the spec warns against). And SEED-15's register shipped with the
cardinality/hash/state checks but without G8-3's full contract: the
open-home rule, owner equality, the `probe_id` hook, and the round-tail
mode P34.33's tail calls and the P38 tail rely on.

## What this ships

- **`scripts/docs/adr-index.sh` local patch (G8-1).** `status_line()`
  replaces `superseded()`: the latest `- **Status:** <Kind> by ADR-NNN …`
  line *inside `## Status updates`* — all five kinds (Superseded /
  Amended / Qualified / Extended / Revisited) — wins over the header
  `Status`. Section-scoped, so trigger-evaluation prose can never rewrite
  the cell. The vendoring banner now names the patch honestly (the
  byte-identical claim was already false). `docs/adr/README.md`
  regenerated: **20 status corrections**.
- **`docs/build/tools/adr_index_check.py` (new).** A byte-identical
  Python port of the generator's parse: regenerates the index in memory
  and diffs the committed README; `—`-cell triage — a violation for
  ADR-146+ (the T1 template boundary) or a field present-but-unparsed,
  a warning only for a genuinely absent legacy field (ADR-120 — the one
  declared warning; the closed owner-label list `Ticket`/`Phase`/
  `Phase / ticket` is honoured, never invented). Plus the G8-2/COV-14
  scan: the named `Supersedes:`/`Amends:`/`Qualifies:`/`Extends:` fields,
  `Amends / qualifies / extends:`, `… landed ADRs:`, `Related:`-family
  parenthetical annotations (a kind word beats a first-person verb),
  and sentence-initial body declarations; `none`, quoted spans,
  `no status line for`, `leaves … unchanged`, records-supersession,
  `not <kind>`, self-refs, bare refs and mechanism notes oblige nothing;
  a named target with no file fails closed. Each satisfying line must sit
  in the target's `## Status updates` with a `(<date>)`.
- **8 appended status lines (the only legal body change).** ADR-030←068
  Amended, ADR-039←054 Extended, ADR-055←069 Amended, ADR-068←091+097
  Extended, ADR-087←088 Superseded, ADR-104←114 Revisited, ADR-105←116
  Amended — each `- **Status:** <Kind> by ADR-NNN (2026-10-05)` plus a
  `Status note` naming the declaring field (the SEED-11d/SEED-12c form).
- **`docs/build/tools/adr_triggers.py` extended (G8-3).** The open-home
  rule `check_backlog.py` applies, judged from the register side: open BL
  row; BL-002's accepted monitor never for `fired-unanswered`; a closed
  row only while quiet/superseded. Register `home` must equal the BL row
  whose `sources` name the ADR. `probe_id` validated as a token when
  present (the G10 hook). `--round-tail <YYYY-MM-DD>` fails any
  `last_evaluated` predating the round and any `fired-unanswered` row
  without an `S1… disposition:` record — P34.33's and the P38 tail's mode.
- **`Makefile` `docs-check-adr`** joins `docs-check`; both tools print
  offered/evaluated counts (SIG-ENG-042).
- **ADR-198** — the owned decisions record (index status source; the
  closed owner-label list and the ADR-120 `—` verdict; the checked
  declaration surface including the Related-family extension beyond the
  spec's named labels; open-home alignment; round-tail + probe hook) —
  plus its Appendix F row (via `spec_src` + BUILD.sh), its BL-084
  sources/title entry, and its register row (quiet at authoring, S6R-24).
- **26 regression tests** (15 trigger + 11 index) — fixture trees, no
  living-record pins (BM-TEST-01); one real-tree validator call per file.

this surface; the `fired-unanswered` triggers the register tracks are the
round tail's, per their own rows.

## Deviations

- **Strict-`—` AC caveat, recorded:** the ticket's literal "0 rows reading
  `—`" cannot be met for ADR-120's owner cell — the file names no
  Ticket/Phase/Phase-ticket field and the body is frozen; inventing an
  owner (or a `Scope:` fallback, or a committed override file) would
  falsify the derived column. The declared warn-only gap stands and every
  *fixable* `—` hard-fails (ADR-198 decision 2 + alternatives; the
  validator's own post-marker viol already enforces the template
  boundary).
- **Declaration surface beyond the spec's named field labels:** the
  Related-family annotation scan and sentence-initial body declarations
  are checked too — the convention's own history treats them as
  line-worthy (ADR-075←081's "departs", ADR-092←099's "this ADR
  supersedes"), and restricting to the named labels would produce exactly
  the "none superseded" reading the spec warns against (ADR-198
  decision 3 + alternatives).
